value.zh: 審配令士卒曰：「堅守死戰！
value.en: Shen Pei told the troops: "Hold the walls and fight to the death!
value.literal: Shen Pei ordered the soldiers: "Hold fast and fight to the death!

value.zh: 操軍疲矣，幽州方至，何憂無主！」
value.en: Cao Cao's army is spent, and reinforcements from You Province are on the way. Why fear that we are leaderless?"
value.literal: Cao Cao's army is exhausted; forces from You Province are just arriving — why worry that there will be no lord!"

value.zh: 操出行圍，配伏弩射之，幾中。
value.en: When Cao Cao rode out to inspect the siege lines, Shen Pei had crossbowmen hidden to shoot at him. The bolts nearly found their mark.
value.literal: When Cao Cao went out on an inspection of the encirclement, Pei hid crossbowmen who shot at him — he was nearly hit.

value.zh: 配兄子榮為東門校尉，八月，戊寅，榮夜開門內操兵。
value.en: Shen Pei's nephew Rong commanded the east gate. On wuyin in the eighth month, Rong opened the gate by night and let Cao Cao's men in.
value.literal: Pei's elder brother's son Rong was Commandant of the East Gate; on the day wuyin in the eighth month, Rong opened the gate by night and admitted Cao Cao's troops.

value.zh: 配拒戰城中，操兵生獲之。
value.en: Shen Pei fought on inside the city until Cao Cao's men captured him alive.
value.literal: Pei resisted in battle within the city, and Cao Cao's troops took him alive.

value.zh: 辛評家系鄴獄，辛毘馳往，欲解之，已悉為配所殺。
value.en: Xin Ping's family was held in the Ye jail. Xin Pi rushed to free them, but Shen Pei had already had them all executed.
value.literal: Xin Ping's family was imprisoned in Ye; Xin Pi galloped there wishing to release them, but they had already all been killed by Pei.

value.zh: 操兵縛配詣帳下，毘逆以馬鞭擊其頭，罵之曰：「奴，汝今日真死矣！」
value.en: Cao Cao's men bound Shen Pei and brought him to headquarters. Xin Pi met him and whipped him across the head, shouting, "You slave — this time you are truly dead!"
value.literal: Cao Cao's troops bound Pei and brought him beneath the tent; Pi went up to him and struck his head with a riding crop, cursing him: "Slave — today you truly die!"

value.zh: 配顧曰：「狗輩，正由汝曹破我冀州，恨不得殺汝也！
value.en: Shen Pei turned and said, "You curs — it was your kind who ruined Ji Province. I only regret I could not kill you!
value.literal: Pei turned and said: "Dog pack — it was precisely you lot who ruined my Ji Province; I only regret I could not kill you!

value.en: And as I still live, can you kill me now?"
value.literal: And can you today kill me while I yet live?"

value.zh: 有頃，操引見，謂配曰：「曩日孤之行圍，何弩之多也！」
value.en: After a time Cao Cao had him brought before him and said, "When I rode the lines the other day, your crossbow bolts came thick as rain."
value.literal: After a while Cao Cao had him brought in and said to Pei: "The other day when I inspected the encirclement, how many crossbow bolts there were!"

value.en: Shen Pei said, "I only regret there were not more."
value.literal: Pei said: "I still regret there were too few!"

value.zh: 操曰：「卿忠於袁氏，亦自不得不爾。」
value.en: Cao Cao said, "You were loyal to the Yuan house. You could not have done otherwise."
value.literal: Cao Cao said: "You were loyal to the Yuans — you could not have acted otherwise."
He intended to spare his life.

value.zh: 配意氣壯烈，終於橈辭，而辛毘等號哭不已，遂斬之。
value.en: Shen Pei remained fierce and unyielding to the end, but Xin Pi and the others kept wailing until Cao Cao ordered his execution.
value.literal: Pei's spirit and bearing were fierce and bold; to the end he would not soften his words — but Xin Pi and the others wept and wailed without cease, and so he was beheaded.

value.zh: 冀州人張子謙先降，素與配不善，笑謂配曰：「正南，卿竟何如我？」
value.en: Zhang Ziqian of Ji Province, who had surrendered earlier and had never been on good terms with Shen Pei, mocked him: "Zhengnan — see how much better I fare than you?"
value.literal: The Ji Province native Zhang Ziqian had surrendered earlier; he had always been on bad terms with Pei and, laughing, said to Pei: "Zhengnan — in the end how do you compare with me?"

value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 145
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 145

value.zh: 魏陳留公主寡居，僕射高肇、秦州刺史張彝皆欲尚之，公主許彝而不許肇。
value.en: The Chenliu princess of Wei was a widow. Grand chancellor Gao Zhao and Zhang Yi, governor of Qin province, both sought to marry her. She favored Zhang Yi and rejected Gao Zhao.
value.literal: The Princess of Chenliu of Wei lived as a widow; Vice Director Gao Zhao and Governor of Qin Province Zhang Yi both wished to marry her; the Princess agreed to Yi but not to Zhao.

value.zh: 肇怒，譖彝於魏主，彝坐沉廢累年。
value.en: Gao Zhao, furious, denounced Zhang Yi to the Wei emperor, and Yi languished in disgrace for years.
value.literal: Zhao was angry, slandered Yi before the Wei ruler; Yi on account of this was demoted and idle for many years.

value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 215
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 215

value.zh: 李林甫領吏部尚書，日在政府，選事悉委侍郎宋遙、苗晉卿。
value.en: Li Linfu held the ministry of personnel and was at the secretariat every day; he entrusted all selections entirely to Vice Ministers Song Yao and Miao Jinqing.
value.literal: Li Linfu held the post of Minister of Personnel and was daily at the Secretariat; all matters of selection he entirely entrusted to Vice Ministers Song Yao and Miao Jinqing.

value.zh: 御史中丞張倚新得幸於上，遙、晉卿欲附之。
value.en: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi had recently won the emperor's favor, and Yao and Jinqing sought his patronage.
value.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi had recently won the emperor's favor, and Yao and Jinqing wished to attach themselves to him.

value.zh: 時選人集者以萬計，入等者六十四人。
value.en: Tens of thousands of candidates had assembled; only sixty-four passed the selection.
value.literal: At the time candidates assembled in numbers of tens of thousands; those who passed into the selected ranks were sixty-four.

value.zh: 倚子奭為之首，群議沸騰。
value.en: Yi's son Shi ranked first, and public outrage erupted.
value.literal: Yi's son Shi ranked first, and public talk seethed.

value.zh: 前薊令蘇孝韞以告安祿山，祿山入言於上，上悉召入等人面試之，奭手持試紙，終日不成一字，時人謂之「曳白」。
value.en: Former prefect of Ji Su Xiaoyun reported the affair to An Lushan, who brought it to the emperor. The emperor summoned all sixty-four passers for a personal examination. Shi held his paper all day and could not write a single character. People called it "dragging a blank sheet."
value.literal: Former Ji Prefect Su Xiaoyun reported it to An Lushan; Lushan entered and spoke of it to the emperor. The emperor summoned all who had passed for a face-to-face examination. Shi held the examination paper in hand and throughout the day could not complete a single character. People of the time called this "dragging a blank."

value.zh: 癸亥，遙貶武當太守，晉卿貶安康太守，倚貶淮陽太守，同考判官禮部郎中裴朏等皆貶嶺南官。
value.en: On guihai day, Yao was demoted to prefect of Wudang, Jinqing to prefect of Ankang, and Yi to prefect of Huaiyang; the co-examiners, including Ministry of Rites section chief Pei Fei, were all sent to posts in Lingnan.
value.literal: On the day guihai, Yao was demoted to Prefect of Wudang, Jinqing to Prefect of Ankang, Yi to Prefect of Huaiyang, and the co-examiners including Ministry of Rites Section Chief Pei Fei were all demoted to posts in Lingnan.
Jinqing was a native of Huguan.
